Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  April 3, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on April 3, 2025. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio
  Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  None

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Services
  Mary Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Human Services Transportation Manager
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner
McLemore that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on
February 6, 2025, be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Padilla, McLemore, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Graffiti Supervisor Gilbert Gonzalez reported the
following: Park Maintenance – staff recently installed two bike racks at Darby Edward
Vincent Parks. We have a third concrete slab that will be installed at Edward Vincent Park.
Tree Maintenance – The city tree crew are working through each district, focusing on trees
that are not scheduled for full trimming until 2027. Any tree requiring immediate attention
will receive a safety trim to ensure proper clearance for pedestrians and vehicles.
Meanwhile, our tree trimming contractor, West Cost Arborists, is completing work along
Pincay and Crenshaw and will begin the annual trimming of ficus trees next week. Graffiti

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Abatement – Imperial and Crenshaw area were heavily tagged as well as Imperial from
Yukon to Crenshaw, and the Darby Dixon area all throughout the small community. Center
Park has been the target of graffiti in the past month. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-
8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Park Supervisor Mary Rouzan reported the following: Youth
Sports - The Inglewood Youth Sports League continues to do big things in the city,
providing top-notch athletic experiences. Spring is in the air, representing a tremendously
busy time for sports. The IYSL basketball league is in Week 9, with playoff games being
played this weekend. The season will have a grand finale, hosting four Championship
games at the Intuit Dome on Thursday, April 10, and Friday, April 11. Not to be outdone,
our youth soccer league is nearing playoffs and will host league championships at
Champions Field on Saturday, April 19th. All Basketball and Soccer players and coaches will
be celebrated on April 16 at the season-end banquet at Edward Vincent Jr. Park. All
participants will receive awards, pictures, food, and closing remarks from coaches. In 2025,
Inglewood Youth Sports returned to competition in the SCMAF (Southern California
Municipal Federation) sports tournaments. Inglewood has a long history of competing to
win in SCMAF, and we accomplished our goal of returning in 2025. We had two flag
football teams compete in the fall. Our “C” team placed third while our “B” team earned
the runner-up trophy. Our basketball teams took their opportunities to another level. We
sent three boys’ basketball teams to compete in the BASE local SCMAF tournament on
March 15. Although our “B” team (fifth & sixth graders) brought home the runner-up
trophy, our “C” team (3rd & 4th graders) and “A” team (7th & 8th graders) came back with
tournament championships! Their success catapulted them into the SCMAF finals
tournament the following weekend with “Free” entry fees due to their winning ways. We
also entered two girls’ teams (“B” and “C”) for the March 22 SCMAF Regional tournaments.
We are proud to report that our boys “A” team (7th & 8th graders) along with our girls’ “C”
team came away with championships! Inglewood is back on the SCMAF map! Just like that!
The Dodgers Dreamteam “Spring” season is “Sold Out” with 192 participants ages 5-8.
They will practice once a week for one hour and play two games weekly (Thursdays &
Saturdays) through June 7. Finally, let us welcome back the sport of Track and Field. A new
offering this spring is proving to be popular with 135 participants. The participants practice
twice a week at the St. Mary’s Academy track and at EVP in preparation for the four-meet
seasons. Schedules and all pertinent information regarding Inglewood Youth Sports can be
found at www.cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com. Summer Day Camp the Parks, Recreation
and Community Services Department has 3 summer camp offerings this year.
Camp Discovery: A STEAM-Based Experience for Early Learners
Camp Discovery is a unique kiddie camp designed for children ages 3 to 5. With a STEAM-
focused theme, campers will participate in hands-on science activities, virtual field trips,
and creative explorations in cooking and theater arts. Activities are designed to inspire

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

curiosity, imagination, and creativity, allowing children to explore their artistic talents and
scientific abilities in a fun and enriching environment.
Camp Location
Siminski Park – 4864 W. 97th Street, Inglewood, CA 90301
Sessions
Camp is offered in four two-week sessions.
Session 1  June 16 – June 27, 2025
Session 2  June 30 – July 11, 2025 (no camp on July 4)
Session 3  July 14 – July 25, 2025
Session 4  July 28 – August 8, 2025
Camp Hours
Day Camp: 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
Cost (includes camp fee, virtual field trips, and T-shirt)
Residents:  $124 per 2-week session
Non Residents:  $225 per 2-week session

Game On: Sports and Adventure Odyssey Get ready for an action-packed summer at
Darby Park! Designed for kid’s ages 6 to 12, this camp is filled with exciting sports activities,
outdoor adventures, and endless fun. Whether you are passionate about sports or eager
for a new challenge, campers will engage in exciting team games, build new skills, and
make lasting friendships. With a focus on sports and adventure, this camp promises
unforgettable experiences and memories that will last a lifetime. Campers will enjoy a
different theme each session, as well as participate in arts and crafts, specialty activities,
field trips, and more!
Camp Location
Darby Park – 3400 W. Arbor Vitae, Inglewood, CA 90305
Sessions
Summer Day Camp is an all-day program available in four two-week sessions. Optional
extended care is offered before and after camp hours.
Session 1  June 16 – June 27, 2025
Session 2  June 30 – July 11, 2025 (no camp on July 4)
Session 3  July 14 – July 25, 2025
Session 4  July 28 – August 8, 2025
Camp Hours
Day Camp: 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
Before and After Care: 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.
Cost for Inglewood Residents
Day Camp (2-weeks) $124 per session (includes camp fee, field trip, and T-shirt) Before
and After Care $28 per session (available for day campers only) Cost for Non-Residents

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

Day Camp (2-weeks) $253 per session (includes camp fee, before and after care, field trip,
and T-shirt)

Adventure Awaits – Let’s Explore it Together! Prepare for an exciting summer adventure
at Rogers Park! Designed for camper’s ages 6 to 12, this camp offers a perfect blend of
recreation and education, ensuring each week is filled with fun and discovery. From
exploring nature to engaging in hands-on science experiments, every activity is designed
to spark curiosity and inspire a love for learning. Through team-building activities, exciting
challenges, and outdoor adventures, campers will develop valuable skills, build confidence,
and create lasting memories. Campers will enjoy a different theme each session, as well
as participate in arts and crafts, specialty activities, field trips, and more! Camp Location
Rogers Park – 400 W. Beach Avenue, Inglewood, CA 90302
Sessions
Summer Day Camp is an all-day program available in four two-week sessions. Optional
extended care is offered before and after camp hours.
Session 1  June 16 – June 27, 2025
Session 2  June 30 – July 11, 2025 (no camp on July 4)
Session 3  July 14 – July 25, 2025
Session 4  July 28 – August 8, 2025
Camp Hours
 Day Camp: 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Before and After Care: 7:00
a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.
Cost for Inglewood Residents
Day Camp (2-weeks) $124 per session (includes camp fee, field trip, and T-shirt. Before
and After Care $28 per session (available for day campers only) Cost for Non-Residents
Day Camp (2-weeks) $253 per session (includes camp fee, before and after care, field trip,
and T-shirt).
Registration
Register online at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org. Registration for Inglewood residents
begins on Monday, April 28, and for non-residents on Monday, May 5, 2025. Camp
registration will be accepted on a first-come, first-served basis and remain open until all
spots are filled.

For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website
at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Transportation Manager Geoffrey Okamoto
reported on the following: Senior Center Operations - Our Senior Center is packed with
more seniors than ever, as we continue to grow our participation numbers, as well as
increase our offerings. Grace Farwell of the organization Helping Elderly Live Productively,

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

or H.E.L.P. for short, will be presenting on the topic of helping seniors improve their ability
to do daily tasks and live independently on April 8. Mercedes Aguirre of the LA County
Department of Mental Health will be conduction a presentation on social isolation on April
14. On April 11, Ally Hernandez from the Water Replenishment District (WRD) will be
hosting a Eco Gardening Workshop. On April 16, Petra Niles of Alzheimer’s Los Angeles will
present on Alzheimer’s. Opicacares will present part two of the behaviors associated with
memory loss on April 24. We are excited to announce new classes, including jewelry
making, acting, and tennis workshops in collaboration with 40 Love at Edward Vincent Jr.
Park. For more information on these classes and to sign up in advance, please see the
reception desk at the Senior Center. On April 10, we will be showing the movie “Summer
of Soul”. On April 18, we will be having an Easter celebration party from 10:00 a.m. to
12:00 p.m., and on April 30, we will be having our quarterly birthday party event. Senior
Nutrition - We are excited to announce the arrival of our new Food Services Program
Manager, Kesha Brady. Kesha comes from an impressive background of management and
grant-funded programs, and we are excited to have her join our team. We serve
approximately 450 seniors weekly through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors
and congregate meals at our Senior Center. We continue to provide fresh produce weekly
in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute, and monthly shelf-stable meal
boxes with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Child and Adult Care Food Program - The Child and
Adult Care Food Program, informally CACFP, serves meals to youth 18 years old and under
and operates at Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The program's hours are
Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. and snacks from
4:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. We serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week. Senior
Transportation - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to provide trips to
seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. During the recent
Cesar Chavez Day holiday, we ran transportation service for dialysis customers to ensure
they could receive their treatments. The transportation department will hire a new full
time and part time paratransit driver to provide added service. We look forward to
continuing to provide the best possible service for our seniors and disabled community.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation, and Community Service Department Director
Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Darby Park Privacy Screen Installation - Our
Parks team recently installed a privacy screen along the fence at Darby Park, extending
from Pincay Street to Arbor Vitae. The green-colored screen was chosen based on
preferences expressed by our landscapers and park visitors. This installation was primarily
implemented to enhance privacy for Renaissance residents. Park Safety Meeting with
Inglewood Police Department - Parks and Recreation Management Staff recently met with
the Inglewood Police Department to review park safety measures and discuss police
response times during incidents at our parks. Captain Oswald and Sergeant Landon
participated in a productive discussion about strategies for improving park safety through
collaboration. Moving forward, we will hold quarterly meetings to assess and strengthen

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission

our park safety initiatives. Inglewood Family Unity Day - Join us for the second Annual
Family Unity Day at Darby Park, hosted by Inglewood District 1 City Councilwoman Gloria
Gray. Families and friends will gather on Saturday, August 26, 2025, from 1:00 p.m. to 6:00
p.m. to enjoy delicious multicultural cuisine, live music, and a fun-filled day of community
engagement. Bring your picnic blankets and lawn chairs for a relaxing day with family and
friends. Details regarding vendor opportunities will be shared as the event date
approaches. Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Newsletter - The "It's All Good
in Inglewood" newsletter will now be published twice a year. The first issue will cover April
through September, featuring spring and summer programs, while the second issue will
cover October through March, highlighting fall and winter activities. The spring and
summer issue will be distributed the first week of April.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown stated that the public is not aware of
how much you do with so little. Congratulations. Commissioner Padilla thanked staff and
asked what we could do to get graffiti down in the city. He suggested a program with the
Inglewood Police Department. Gilbert Gonzalez stated previously that there was a D.A.R.E.
Program. Thomas Uwal stated they will work on collecting more data to analyze.
Commissioner McLemore also thanked staff and welcomed the new employees.
Commissioner Beck thanked the Staff and welcomed new employees. He stated that we
talked about tough things tonight, but parks are safer, and the fruits of everyone’s labor
are shown. He is excited to be at the parks more and is excited for seniors to get out.
Commissioner Denmon, a 50-year resident, stated that the Parks have never looked better
or seemed safer. He asked how Gala was. Thomas Uwal noted this was the second year of
the Gala, and by far, it was one of the best events. The Mayor and the Council stopped by.
The seniors felt so special. Commissioner Denmon asked that flyers and warning signs be
put out to warn patrons in the park about coyotes. Commissioner Beck stated the Pincay
parking lot at Darby Park is being used for tailgating. He suggested having someone
monitor the lot and put up signage.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at 7:10 p.m.
